findings.title: Index creation without CONCURRENTLY locks writes on a large table
findings.explanation: A plain CREATE INDEX on Postgres takes a SHARE lock on `events`, blocking all INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE for the duration of the build. Events is typically a high-write, large table, so this can cause an outage or request pile-up during deploy. Use `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS events_project_id_idx ON events (project_id, id DESC);`. Note that CONCURRENTLY cannot run inside a transaction block, so make sure the migration tool is configured to run this migration outside a transaction (e.g. a no-transaction directive or flag). If the build fails it can leave an INVALID index, so document checking and dropping it before retrying.

findings.title: Migration is not idempotent / re-runnable
findings.explanation: Without `IF NOT EXISTS`, a retried or partially applied migration (or an environment where the index was already created manually as a hotfix) will fail. Add `IF NOT EXISTS`. Also consider whether a down/rollback migration (`DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF EXISTS events_project_id_idx;`) is expected by the repo's convention.

findings.title: No evidence the index matches the query or improves it
findings.explanation: The PR claims the endpoint does a sequential scan, but the query is not in the diff and no EXPLAIN (ANALYZE) output is provided. Please attach before/after plans. Verify the actual query filters on `project_id` and orders by `id DESC` (and that pagination uses keyset on `id`, e.g. `id < :cursor`). If the query also filters by event type or date range, or orders by `created_at`, this index will not fully serve it and a different composite index may be needed. A sequential scan can also be chosen on small tables or low-selectivity projects regardless of the index.

findings.title: Check for redundant existing indexes and write overhead
findings.explanation: If an index on `events (project_id)` already exists, the new composite index makes it redundant (it can serve the same prefix lookups), so consider dropping it in a follow-up to reduce write amplification and storage. Also note that the new index adds write cost to every event insert, which is worth mentioning in the PR description along with the expected index size.

findings.title: Missing trailing newline / naming consistency
findings.explanation: Ensure the file ends with a newline and that the index name follows the repo's naming convention (e.g. `idx_events_project_id_id_desc`). The current name `events_project_id_idx` does not reflect the `id DESC` column and could be confused with a single-column index on `project_id`.

```diff

new file mode 100644
index 0000000..0586576
--- /dev/null
+++ b/migrations/005_events_project_idx.sql
@@ -0,0 +1 @@
+CREATE INDEX events_project_id_idx ON events (project_id, id DESC);
```

Before answering, check the change specifically for: authorization and tenant isolation; race conditions and concurrent requests; database migration safety on large tables and during rolling deploys; API changes that break existing clients; retries and idempotency of side effects such as payments; date and time handling; injection; sensitive data in logs; pagination and boundary conditions.

Report every problem you would raise in a code review, from blocking issues to nits. Respond with only a JSON object, no prose before or after it:

Use an empty findings list if you would approve the pull request as it is. Write the review in English.
